tool_input.notes: M.G.L. c. 186, § 12 sets notice periods for ending a tenancy at will. Either party can end it with three months' written notice, or with notice equal to the rent-payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. For nonpayment of rent, the landlord can give 14 days' notice to quit. In some cases the tenant can stop the termination by paying the rent owed. These are notice and cure procedures. The section does not limit the reasons a landlord may use to end or not renew a tenancy, since a tenancy at will can be ended without cause. So it is not a just-cause eviction rule, and it does not fit any other category: rent increase limits, security deposits, application or screening fees, screening restrictions, or algorithmic rent setting. No rules were recorded.
